note: A RATCHET, not a target. The gate fails when errors RISE above this, never when they merely stay put. A hard zero would block every commit today; a ratchet stops the regression that actually happened -- a format-string rule that was never called survived two commits because nothing compiled the 23 modules it broke.
lower_me: When errors fall, lower this. That is the whole mechanism.
why_the_totals_moved: 24 modules, not 25: `Stream` is a sub-block and has no standalone form -- its define_registers is typed on its PARENT's State, so emitting it alone produced a `self` with nothing to bind to. It is still compiled, inside the module it belongs to. The error count held at 27 across a change that added 275 lines of newly emitted code: every module that compiled before has the same count it had, and the 4 that appeared are all `cortexm`, which previously emitted nothing at all because an empty method body returned silently.
